We've been looking into using the LSP highlighting from the Waterproof Genre. I have come to an LLM-coded solution, and I'd like to check if we're walking an okay path with this:

The first step was just adding Subverso Highlighted support in, which got us variable name highlighting. The second step added an LSP handler that added the keywords and such.

I'm okay having a bit of tech debt on our end to get this to work, I just want to check:

  1. Am I missing a way to get all tokens from the LSP to begin with?
  2. Am I missing a clean way to use more of Verso to do this?

The current fix is available at https://github.com/impermeable/waterproof-genre/tree/d10c520f575257d35ba6ace398e243469ef80cb0 along with a testing script to get the tokens.

cc @Tammo

Verso's LSP support doesn't go through SubVerso's highlighting at all. It just delegates to the Lean LSP server's built-in support for semantic tokens, which is based on the info trees, and then augments the response with its own tokens. I'd encourage you to adopt an approach like that, which ought to have much lower latency.

See https://github.com/leanprover/verso/blob/b0241198570de77dbbd3607a8faa0a1cb97b92b0/src/verso/Verso/Doc/Lsp.lean#L392-L574 for how Verso does it.

Ah, a quick glance at that tree shows something similar, not going through SubVerso.

This looks like it's actually working around an upstream Verso issue. Is that right? If so, we should fix it there. Chaining semantic token handlers isn't great - the delta-coding used in LSP means that we have to decode and re-encode all tokens in a response, so there's overhead linear in the number of tokens _for each chained handler_. This is not so good for a latency-sensitive response. Can we make the Verso one better so you just have to tweak a setting somewhere or add to a table of some kind?

I think the X-Y here is that we're working around https://github.com/leanprover/verso/issues/135 not existing in Verso. I'm happy to eat the higher latency until we have that, even if it takes a bit. What we're doing now is definitely very hacky, so I wouldn't expose stuff to hook into based on this.

Interesting - why is this needed here?

What I'd expect you're doing is, within the scope of some kind of container, concatenating the contents of the Lean blocks and then elaborating them, which should result in a complete info tree. I wouldn't expect it to require special handling.

Are you elaborating some other way?

So before I started messing around with the highlighting, this was how we elaborated.

My initial thought was that the issue there was that we're not actually passing the blocks into the multilean block here.

Refactoring (with LLM-support) brought me here: https://github.com/impermeable/waterproof-genre/blob/3b4fe3e6069849d072bf2057659f23ac62f03b02/WaterproofGenre.lean#L55 In this state, we can get the information to highlight the variables, but not the keywords.

Pim Otte said:

I think the X-Y here is that we're working around https://github.com/leanprover/verso/issues/135 not existing in Verso. I'm happy to eat the higher latency until we have that, even if it takes a bit. What we're doing now is definitely very hacky, so I wouldn't expose stuff to hook into based on this.

I think indeed that we could implement that feature the way David suggests, and shouldn't take too long. More concretely we just need to create a source map with the verso explanations so we pass it to the lean code block elaborator.

That'd be cool indeed!

By the way, this would still have the problem of incremental reporting you were mentioning before.
I'm myself happy to put some cycles and implement 135 together as I can see this being useful for blueprints.

The concrete idea if you want to give it a try would be:

  • in the multilean directive, collect code blocks and explanations, with a position anchor
  • extend the inline lean elaborator with a new parameter which has the explanations, position-based map
  • have the inline lean elaborator insert the right things at the right place, this could be a bit more tricky due to tactic processing, whereas the elaborator's loop is now command based

I'd dare to say that Codex would work with the examples and the above instructions towards a first prototype.

I think I'm missing still too much of an internal view on verso to get to a quality implementation for Verso itself. If you have a prototype I'll of course happily try it out and I might be able to take it from there:)
@Pim Otte just to be sure, you'd be happy for now with a prototype of the spec in 135 right?
Yeah, at least to my understanding, I would be. The aim would be to use the multilean directive from verso in our Genre and toss the one in our repo.
2026-03-12_17-04-45_chromium_multilean-review-chromium.png
A very rough Codex-built prototype but should be a basis for further work, branch at https://github.com/ejgallego/verso/tree/feat/issue-135-multilean
Likely the main thing to fix is that we may want to update Subverso to support this style better, but I think David knows better.

Did a quick test based on that, and functionality wise it matches https://github.com/impermeable/waterproof-genre/blob/3b4fe3e6069849d072bf2057659f23ac62f03b02/WaterproofGenre.lean#L55 (i.e. We're not getting keywords like have and let from the LSP, but we are getting variables.)
So you are getting semantic tokens, but incomplete?

I confirm the problem, I think it was known, better integration with the embedded syntax and semantic tokens is missing, upstream uses a combined Ast / infotree walk. The Ast walk is missing, the infotree is not, this is why you see variables only.

Yep, that's right. That being said, I'm not sure if we ought to be able to get them all in the way I'm trying to right now. I'm using the lsp_tokens.py script here: https://github.com/impermeable/waterproof-genre/tree/debug/upsteam-multilean (currently with the Simple.lean file on that branch as well)

I think there is a reasonable workaround until we land a full fix in Verso: have you elaborator push a custom infotree node with the syntax and amend the LSP handler to imitate what Lean does, I will post a POC in a few mins.

I'd dare to say a Lean-level fix is preferred vs ad-hoc syntax slicing in Python.

Here's a POC: https://github.com/ejgallego/verso/tree/fix/semantic-inline-tokens

Due to the API surface affected, instead of trying to ship the improvement locally in Waterproof, I'd suggest to put cycles towards verifying David is OK with this approach and merging in Verso itself.
Of course let me know if that solves your issue!
I'm actually getting only import, open and #doc as tokens with a very simple Verso file on that branch (and not any contents of fenced lean blocks), so maybe it's tossing some stuff along the way?
Let me check more carefully, the test content is super hard to decode due to semanticsToken encoding.

In the test case included in the branch I get:

  - def at line 11, cols 0..2 as keyword
  - let at line 11, cols 16..18 as keyword
  - y at line 11, col 20 as variable
  - y at line 11, col 28 as variable
  - theorem at line 12, cols 0..6 as keyword
  - by at line 12, cols 27..28 as keyword
  - trivial at line 13, cols 2..8 as keyword

for the lean code:

  def blockVal := let y := 1; y
  theorem blockThm : True := by
    trivial

Does that look correct to you?

Ah, maybe the problem is that you need the lsp server to fully sync, this is a known issue, this could explain you getting partial results.

Actually Marc and Sebastian explained this to me recently (I'm glad), Lean tries to stream the semanticsToken in a particular way due to LSP limitations. Can your use case wait for the full file to be processed, or do you need more incremental output?

Mmmm, maybe. If we need to wait for the whole file, I think we definitely would need to supplement it with our own grammar to highlight. If we get it incrementally we might be able to do without that. (But if it's a known issue with perspective on a fix, I have time to wait for that:))

I think you should be able to use the incremental support, but note that Lean deviates a bit from LSP. Happy to help with this, the expert is Marc.

So far everything seems to work fine on my side, don't hesitate to provide the problematic example and a trace log (you can get that easily using the Verso / Lean LSP testing framework, see example in branch)

Questions for @David Thrane Christiansen :

  • semantic tokens: are you OK with keeping inline lean syntax as an infotree extension?
  • multilean: should we update Subverso to support the annotations natively?

Saving the syntax in a custom infotree node is definitely reasonable, this keeps it out of the olean which is good. Or we could preprocess the syntax using the language server's syntactic highlighting, and then just save the tokens directly in the infotree - I'm a bit more inclined to do this, because it avoids repeating some work, but we'd have to profile to really know.

Which SubVerso updates would be needed?

I don't know exactly what went wrong when testing, at least part of the problem was that I messed up merging both branches. That being said, I can now confirm that @Emilio Jesús Gallego Ariass two branches jointly provide the functionality we're looking for:D

@Emilio Jesús Gallego Arias We have a branch that uses your fixes in progress, and @Tammo noticed that the literals and comments are still missing from the semantic tokens. Could it be that those are still missing in https://github.com/ejgallego/verso/tree/fix/semantic-inline-tokens ?

Lean doesn't generally send semantic tokens for comments or all literals. The expectation is that editor clients also implement their own syntax-driven highlighting for those things that are feasible to highlight with a simple lexer (literals and comments), while things like keywords or the distinction between local variables and global constants that require deeper knowledge of the language are provided by the server.

On the other hand, if it’s useful for Waterproof (which I can imagine it might be), it could be interesting to experiment with a small LSP plugin that enriches the current semantic tokens to include comments and literals.

But the LSP spec agrees with what David has said: comments are typically not to be included in LSP semantic tokens. But LSP may fall short of the needs of such a rich editor like Waterproof.
I imagine there's a non-negligable performance impact to include them if the LSP spec explicitly excludes these, so we'll probably want to do these client side then.

I guess it'd depend on how fast the client is. I could see some clients having very efficient support for this, others not so much.

The nice thing about Lean's LSP server is that it is super easy to extend, so only files needing the extension would pay the extra semantic tokens cost.

IIRC the current semantics token implementation already traverses the full Ast, so the overhead would be mainly in the cost of assembling the representation needed client side.

IIRC the big concern is latency. Syntactic fontification is available immediately, while semantic tokens have to wait for elaboration. It's nice to have your comments in comment font while scrolling ahead of the elaborator.
Oh indeed latency is very important too, and not so good in the server side.
I've been re-thinking lately how one would integrate Verso with a WSYWYG editor, still didn't converge, but that's an interesting problem.

I tried refactoring our code a bit more to make more use of the facilities in @Emilio Jesús Gallego Ariass branches, and I'm running into a small snag. I'm not sure this is something we want to have upstream in Verso, but our main use case for multilean is being able to write the following:

::::multilean ```lean def ex : 5 = 5 := by ``` :::input ```lean sorry ``` ::: ```lean done ``` ::::

This allows us to mark the input area for students.

Using multilean from https://github.com/ejgallego/verso/tree/feat/issue-135-multilean the whole input directive is commented, including the lean block contained in it.

I vibecoded a patch for us at https://github.com/impermeable/waterproof-genre/tree/feature/smaller-genre which involves rolling our own multilean block and special-casing the input directive.

This definitely does not make sense for the Manual genre, but something like descending into other blocks to find lean blocks to parse might? As is, I'd be totally happy to keep the above code in our Genre, it feels far less hacky than what we had before, I'm just mentioning it in case it's helpful for finalizing the multilean feature.
That's great feedback Pim, I think such a mechanism is important, in particular for student exercises. Where does it belong, that I'm not sure.
I'd dare to say that for now, keeping it local to your Genre is fine.
We do some special-casing like this in various libraries, like the multi-Lean-module directive leanModules in the reference manual. I think that's an OK thing to do.
